newsitem.title: FRANCE: French poll puts centre-right narrowly ahead.
newsitem.headline: French poll puts centre-right narrowly ahead.

text.p: Following are the results of an opinion poll conducted by Louis Harris on April 25-26 for magazine Politique Opinion and LCI television:

Harris said that 18 percent expressed no opinion. Fully 30 percent said they could change their mind before the May 25-June 1 parliamentary election, while 70 percent said they were sure of their choice.
The poll was based on a survey of 1,004 individuals aged 18 and over. Only the preferences of the 889 individuals who said they were both inscribed on voter lists and certain to vote were counted.

Harris also found that 47 percent of those surveyed said they would prefer a Socialist-Communist majority in the National Assembly while 43 percent said they wanted the centre-right to remain in power.
Another 10 percent said they wanted neither to command an absolute majority while five percent had no opinion.
